hdr.p1: CDMX, Mexico  ·  English B1 · B2 technical reading/writing
hdr.p2: Senior Backend Engineer and Tech Lead with 10+ years in backend development and distributed systems. Today my signature is reliability and automation as a product: a blameless post-mortem system, a monthly uptime methodology (99.95% in July 2026), runbooks, and n8n / spec-driven pipelines that replace manual operations. Generative AI (Claude, Gemini, OpenAI) is the copilot of my SDLC through Spec-Driven Development — ~40% less code review time and 80% autonomous N1 resolution — on Python · PostgreSQL · AWS, with technical leadership of international GK POS rollouts across Latin America.
aim.li1: Leading Service Support engineering at Podemos Progresar (fintech): AI-native incident resolution with SDD.
aim.li2: Running my projects locally with Docker; observability via Grafana.
aim.li3: Pushing my English toward B2 (Quick Learning, in progress).
aim.p1: I work AI-native: Generative AI is the central copilot of my SDLC, not an afterthought. My practice is Spec-Driven Development (SDD/OpenSpec) — the spec is the source of truth, and every change flows through versioned artifacts before a line of code is written.
aim.li4: Automate > operate. Rule of two: any manual report or task done more than twice becomes a spec-driven pipeline.
aim.li5: Reliability as a product. Downtime is measured by real user impact, not by ticket closure; blameless post-mortems; least-privilege runbooks.
aim.li6: State outside the code. IDs, cut-offs and thresholds live in configuration (JSON / Notion) read alike by the workflow and the dashboard — the spec is the contract.
aim.li7: Cursor over ingestion, not the clock. Designed for failure (missed runs, late data), not for the happy path.
aim.p2: Requirements and verifiable scenarios drive the work. AI generates specs, analyzes code statically and proposes implementations against the contract — cutting review cycles by ~40%.
aim.p3: Claude (Anthropic), Gemini, OpenAI and Bedrock across the loop: spec generation, automated debugging, RCA & post-mortems, technical documentation, and an AI Skill for automatic ticket routing with human review on low confidence — driving team adoption.
aim.p4: Agentic workflows with RAG and AI agents. This very site ships structured JSON-LD and a /llms.txt so agents and LLMs can read my profile directly.

proj.p1: ★ 100% built with Spec-Driven Development (SDD/OpenSpec) — the spec is the source of truth in every project.
proj.p2: Multi-business digital loyalty platform: customers collect stamps via QR with nothing to install. Five actors (guest, registered customer, cashier, owner/manager, platform admin), multi-business wallet, tiers and redemptions, self-service business onboarding, KPIs/analytics, satisfaction surveys and a scheduled monthly platform report (pg_cron). All business rules live in PostgreSQL: multi-tenant RLS, RPC in PL/pgSQL SECURITY DEFINER, QR tokens with TTL + SHA-256 fingerprint against replay, rate limiting on anonymous functions, PII-free audit log and feature flags (global + per-business override). Core journeys validated by product in real coffee shops. Ships with an architecture review package (pieces, where each rule lives, deployment, scale limits) for external reviewers. 100% SDD/OpenSpec with 5 specialized AI agents and 28 journeys with twin runbooks.
proj.p3: Self-hosted observability stack (Grafana + Docker) with a single pane over three sources: AWS serverless (Lambda invocations/errors/duration + S3) via CloudWatch, local Docker containers (CPU/memory/health), and Trackion's tickets & SLA. Automated collection with n8n + a read-only IAM role. 100% SDD/OpenSpec.
proj.p4: Multi-tenant, white-label SaaS for EV charging-station operators: live station status over WebSocket (polling fallback), tenant isolation via PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS), RBAC (superadmin/org_admin/operator/viewer) + SSO (OIDC), analytics (uptime, kWh, CSV export), an auditable state scheduler and an installable PWA. 100% SDD/OpenSpec.
proj.p5: White-label serverless help desk: end-to-end ticketing (categorize, prioritize, assign, history; open→in_progress→resolved→closed), admin-managed catalogs, and an open API-integration module (generic inbound webhooks + outbound domain-event dispatch) to plug any external system without touching the core. Grafana tickets & SLA dashboards. 100% SDD/OpenSpec; runs locally via Docker.
proj.p6: Serverless pizza-ordering demo with live order tracking: build your pizza, place the order and watch it move recibido→preparando→horno→listo→entregado in ~70s over WebSocket, driven by a Step Functions Express workflow. Orders in DynamoDB, fully documented OpenAPI/Swagger, frontend on S3 + CloudFront. 100% SDD/OpenSpec. Demo only — no real payments.
proj.p7: Full-stack streetwear/sneakers e-commerce deployed on AWS: JWT auth, product catalog, cart, checkout, Click & Collect, wishlist and an admin dashboard. API on API Gateway + Lambda; frontend on S3 + CloudFront. 100% SDD/OpenSpec.
proj.p8: ETL middleware that automates master-data integration into GK Software retail systems: watches directories, transforms Excel → GK XML across four interfaces (stores, operators, promotions) and transmits via SFTP/FTP — with a Flask web panel (config, operation, audit), a scheduler and SQLite auditing. Re-engineered under SDD/OpenSpec: idempotent single-pass pipeline, pooled SFTP/SQLite connections, and security hardening (parameterized/whitelisted SQL, secrets out of the repo).

wri.h31: Spec-Driven Development: the spec is the source of truth
